name: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion
label: Matador
lede: Three guys, no bass player and a theremin: a Pussy Galore veteran, a kid from Appleton, Wisconsin and a drummer from Queens turned the blues into a sweaty New York noise machine, and got Beck, the Beastie Boys, R.L. Burnside and Weird Al to come along.

eras.title: After Pussy Galore, a trio with no bass
eras.text: Jon Spencer had already spent five years in Pussy Galore, the Washington-born, New York-hardened band that covered the Rolling Stones' entire Exile on Main St. on a dare. When it ended in 1990 he found two players through the New York band The Honeymoon Killers, and the three started jamming with two guitars, drums and no bass at all.

years.src: Wikipedia: Pussy Galore · Wikipedia: Jon Spencer
years.h: Pussy Galore breaks up after Historia de la Musica Rock
years.p: Jon Spencer's first band [[Pussy Galore|cf97d78e-7c86-4931-92c0-b8e22bae1e33]] ends in 1990 after its last album. Spencer starts [[Boss Hog|57648c1f-335d-4216-ba82-508b23b3bcf4]] with Cristina Martinez, his wife since 1989, and keeps looking for something rawer.
years.xp: Pussy Galore started in 1985 with Spencer and Julia Cafritz, fellow Brown University students, and moved to New York in May 1986. Along the way it covered Exile on Main St. front to back on a limited cassette, reportedly on a dare from [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]]. Guitarist Neil Hagerty left for [[Royal Trux|87e27246-8c40-407f-bfb3-5dc416557eeb]].

years.h: Jon Spencer, Judah Bauer and Russell Simins stumble together
years.p: Guitarist [[Judah Bauer|19c21a31-c2f6-446d-b989-f714715a836c]], from Appleton, Wisconsin, and drummer [[Russell Simins|f20a46bf-6f35-4bce-9fbb-b19de6fc3c0b]], from Queens, meet Jon Spencer through [[The Honeymoon Killers|e2bf68b6-5001-4b11-9cfe-64ceed3c281e]]. Spencer said they just kind of stumbled into each other.

years.cap: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion · via Discogs
years.h: Fourteen songs in three hours with Kramer
years.p: The Blues Explosion's first session, with producer [[Kramer|d898e082-70d1-4a86-ac8e-ecdf89892994]] at Noise New York, cuts fourteen songs in three hours with almost no overdubs.
years.xp: A second session followed that winter with [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] at Waterfront in Hoboken, New Jersey. The Kramer tapes leaked out first as a bootleg, A Reverse Willie Horton, pressed in the hundreds on the Public Pop Can label, with a negative image of Clarence Thomas's swearing-in on the cover.

years.h: The first album, stitched from the Kramer and Albini tapes
years.p: Caroline in the US and Hut in the UK release The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion, built from the Kramer and [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] sessions. Germany's Crypt puts out a different cut, Crypt Style.

eras.title: Matador turns up the width
eras.text: Matador signed the band for America and held on to them for a decade. In two years they went from Memphis studio weekends to British television, an Australian tour with Beck and Orange, the record that made the Blues Explosion the most talked-about live act in indie rock.

years.h: Extra Width, cut in Memphis and New York
years.p: The Blues Explosion's first Matador album was recorded at Doug Easley's studio in Memphis and Waterworks in New York. It opens with Afro and runs 36 minutes.

q: The best live band I've ever seen.
years.h: First TV spot, on Channel 4's The Word
years.p: The Blues Explosion play Afro and History of Sex on the UK show The Word. Presenter Mark Lamarr tells the country they're the best live band he's seen.
years.xp: It was the band's first television appearance anywhere. Afro came out as a UK 7-inch that June, with a video by drummer and filmmaker Tom Surgal.

years.h: On the road in Australia and New Zealand with Beck
years.p: The Blues Explosion tour Australia and New Zealand with Beck in August 1994. Beck would later remix them.

years.h: A stink bomb kills the first live album in Tucson
years.p: An attempt to record a live album at the DPC in Tucson, Arizona is abandoned when someone in the crowd throws a stink bomb.

years.h: Orange: strings, theremin and pure swagger
years.p: Matador releases Orange. Bellbottoms opens with a string arrangement by Kurt Hoffman, and Pitchfork later called the album an absurd burst of swagger and libido.
years.xp: The Village Voice's critics' poll and NME both put Orange at No. 16 for 1994. Bellbottoms went into The Pitchfork 500 and, decades later, opened Edgar Wright's film Baby Driver.

eras.title: Beasties, Burnside and Weird Al
eras.text: Orange opened every door at once. The Blues Explosion toured with the Beastie Boys, handed their songs to a crowd of remixers, drove to a farm in Mississippi to back a 69-year-old bluesman, and got a video directed by Weird Al Yankovic.

years.cap: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion · via Discogs
years.h: Opening for the Beastie Boys, with The Roots on the bill
years.p: The Blues Explosion play UK shows with the [[Beastie Boys|9beb62b2-88db-4cea-801e-162cd344ee53]] in March 1995, then a US tour with them and [[The Roots|80b3cf5e-18fe-4c59-98c7-e5bb87210710]] in May.

years.h: Beck, Mike D, Moby and GZA remix the band
years.p: Matador's Experimental Remixes EP hands Blues Explosion songs to Beck, [[Mike D|d3126097-d402-448a-80de-b863c34c735f]], [[Moby|8970d868-0723-483b-a75b-51088913d3d4]], UNKLE, Dub Narcotic Sound System, and GZA with Killah Priest.

years.cap: R.L. Burnside, A Ass Pocket of Whiskey (1996)
years.h: Backing R.L. Burnside at a Mississippi farm
years.p: At Lunati Farms in Holly Springs, Mississippi, the trio records A Ass Pocket of Whiskey with bluesman [[R.L. Burnside|355eed00-6c40-4d33-940a-600b2597407a]] and his guitarist Kenny Brown.
years.xp: Two more songs from the same day, Alice Mae and Highway 7, ended up on Burnside's 1997 album Mr. Wizard. The session sat in the middle of the band's own recording week for Now I Got Worry, which moved between Memphis, Los Angeles and Tucson.

years.h: Billboard: Orange has sold 70,000 copies
years.p: By September 1996, according to Billboard, Orange has sold 70,000 copies, big numbers for a Matador band with no bass player.

years.h: Now I Got Worry, with Rufus Thomas on vocals
years.p: Memphis soul great [[Rufus Thomas|af1f46fe-903c-4bbf-8e20-a3e114343bd0]] sings on the album and [[Money Mark|9641c354-53da-4fd5-b8ee-d52e8e1e7e7e]] plays keys on three songs. Now I Got Worry reaches No. 50 in the UK.

years.h: Weird Al Yankovic directs the Wail video
years.p: The video for Wail, from Now I Got Worry, is directed by [[Weird Al Yankovic|7746d775-9550-4360-b8d5-c37bd448ce01]], of all people.

years.h: On tour with R.L. Burnside across Europe and the US
years.p: The Blues Explosion take [[R.L. Burnside|355eed00-6c40-4d33-940a-600b2597407a]] on the Now I Got Worry tour through the UK, Europe and the US in October and November 1996.
years.xp: Dutch TV filmed a pre-show jam at the Melkweg in Amsterdam on October 23, and the footage became the video for Boogie Chillun. Six days later they cut a live session at MTV's London studios.

eras.title: Everybody wants to remix the blues
eras.text: The band got bigger, stranger and more collaborative. A promo live record named after a Public Enemy song, a studio album run through half a dozen producers, and a music video where movie stars played the band.

years.h: Controversial Negro, a promo-only live record
years.p: Controversial Negro, named after a [[Public Enemy|bf2e15d0-4b77-469e-bfb4-f8414415baca]] song, comes out as a promotional live album: vinyl in the US, CD in the UK, and an official release in Japan with five extra tracks.

years.h: Acme: Albini, Dan the Automator and more at the desk
years.p: Matador releases Acme, with [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]], [[Dan the Automator|33945eeb-e2d2-4257-a199-661cbadcf8af]], [[Calvin Johnson|cac7a688-14a8-46c3-8fc8-11cca866677c]], Jim Dickinson and Alec Empire among the producers and mixers.
years.xp: Work began with Dan the Automator on a cover of Dr. John's Right Place, Wrong Time for the Scream 2 soundtrack, and the core sessions ran at Albini's Electrical Audio in Chicago in January 1998. A companion EP of B-sides and remixes, Xtra-Acme USA, followed in 1999.

years.cap: Talk About the Blues video, dir. Evan Bernard
years.h: Winona Ryder plays Jon Spencer in a video
years.p: In Evan Bernard's video for Talk About the Blues, actors Winona Ryder, Giovanni Ribisi and John C. Reilly play the Blues Explosion while the real band turns up as detectives.

years.h: Van robbed in Vancouver; Spencer's 1962 theremin is gone
years.p: The tour van is broken into at a Sheraton in Vancouver. Among the stolen gear is Jon Spencer's original 1962 Vanguard theremin, never recovered.

years.h: Sideways Soul, with Dub Narcotic Sound System
years.p: K Records releases Sideways Soul: Dub Narcotic Sound System Meets The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion in a Dancehall Style!, made with [[Calvin Johnson|cac7a688-14a8-46c3-8fc8-11cca866677c]]'s crew.

eras.title: Plastic Fang, Damage and a long rest
eras.text: The trio worked with outside producers and new labels, shortened its own name for one album, and backed Solomon Burke and Tom Waits along the way. Then, after playing Orange start to finish in London, it stopped.

years.h: Plastic Fang, produced by Steve Jordan
years.p: Session drummer and producer Steve Jordan produces Plastic Fang, the Blues Explosion's last Matador album. She Said gets a video by Floria Sigismondi.
years.xp: The band played Later... with Jools Holland on the BBC that April. A second She Said video was shot at London's 100 Club on Oxford Street.

years.h: Backing Solomon Burke at the Royal Festival Hall
years.p: Soul singer [[Solomon Burke|d5c79890-36c5-4f1b-bed3-4468eee093f3]] shares the Royal Festival Hall stage in London with the Blues Explosion for a one-off show.

years.h: Damage, as just the Blues Explosion
years.p: On Sanctuary Records, Damage is the only album credited to the shortened name Blues Explosion. [[Chuck D|88633ac3-c8e2-420f-8415-77ac56b3105f]] guests on Hot Gossip.

years.h: The theme for Anthony Bourdain's No Reservations
years.p: The Blues Explosion record about a minute of music for Anthony Bourdain's Travel Channel show No Reservations; around 20 seconds is used in the opening.

years.h: Orange played in full at KOKO, London
years.p: At an All Tomorrow's Parties Don't Look Back show at KOKO in London, the Blues Explosion play Orange start to finish, then a second set.

years.h: The Blues Explosion go on hiatus
years.p: After touring Damage through 2004 and 2005, including Japan with [[The Kills|2c629b8c-d751-4131-b785-5690bb5e0fd7]] and UK dates supporting [[The Hives|487bfd74-71bf-46dd-b89c-80b7a0f06f2f]], the trio stops.

eras.title: Back from the dead, with bonus tracks
eras.text: The Blues Explosion came back quietly with a secret show, then loudly with a reissue campaign that finally put the whole catalog back in print. Two more albums followed before one last show in Germany.

years.h: A secret show at the Bowery Electric
years.p: The trio plays a secret show at New York's Bowery Electric and the NYC Bicycle Film Festival, then tours Europe that August and September.

years.h: Dirty Shirt Rock 'n' Roll and the expanded reissues
years.p: Shout! Factory's campaign puts out a 22-track retrospective, Dirty Shirt Rock 'n' Roll: The First Ten Years, and expanded editions of the old albums; the Now I Got Worry reissue doubles to 32 tracks.

years.h: Black Betty for a Volkswagen Super Bowl ad
years.p: The Blues Explosion record a cover of Black Betty in Australia for a Volkswagen commercial that airs during the Super Bowl.

years.h: Meat + Bone, the first album in eight years
years.p: The first Blues Explosion album since Damage draws raves from Pitchfork, Mojo and The Quietus. That March they played Jeff Mangum's All Tomorrow's Parties in Minehead.

years.h: Freedom Tower, a love letter to old New York
years.p: Freedom Tower: No Wave Dance Party 2015 becomes the Blues Explosion's final studio album.

years.h: The last show: Nuremberg, Germany
years.p: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion play what turns out to be their final show, in Nuremberg on March 18, 2016.

eras.title: Nipped in the bud
eras.text: No one announced a breakup at first. Then Jon Spencer explained what had happened: Judah Bauer's health had ended the touring life, and the band with it.

years.h: Bellbottoms opens Baby Driver
years.p: Edgar Wright uses Bellbottoms from Orange in his film Baby Driver, and a new generation finds the Blues Explosion.

q: Everything got nipped in the bud when Judah got sick.
years.h: Jon Spencer says Judah Bauer's illness ended the band
years.p: Jon Spencer tells the South Bend Tribune the Blues Explosion is done: Judah Bauer developed a respiratory problem and can't go out on a rock and roll tour.
years.xp: Spencer said that for multiple reasons it became clear the band was probably over. He went solo that year, then toured as Jon Spencer and the HITmakers with Sam Coomes and [[Janet Weiss|ede4e405-0715-4340-b612-ce79675d4133]].

years.h: Jon Spencer: the Blues Explosion is no more
years.p: Jon Spencer states plainly that the Jon Spencer Blues Explosion is finished, after being on hiatus since the 2016 Nuremberg show.
